title: squad — a developer, a reviewer on another provider, and a designer, all on small models
summary: three roles on one issue: Claude builds, astra reviews the code, Sonnet reviews the experience; the PR merges itself once both approve
description: One issue carries the auto-merge label, so the whole loop runs without you: the developer (Sonnet) implements and opens a PR, then labels the issue ready-for-review, which dispatches two reviewers into worktrees cut from the developer's branch — a tech lead on codex/astra reading the code, and a designer on Sonnet walking the README and the command line as a newcomer. A reviewer that wants something changed nudges the developer, whose fix nudges both reviewers back. When both have approved the PR's current head, the developer runs `weawr merge`, which checks the label and the verdicts and merges. The second issue has no auto-merge label: the same review round happens, and the merge is yours.

issues.title: `tally top [n]` — the most counted names
issues.body:
With a few dozen names in the tally, `list` is too long to glance at. I want the leaders.

**Ask:** `tally top` prints the three most counted names and their counts; `tally top 10` prints ten. Ties are broken by name, the way `list` already orders them.

**Acceptance**
- `tally top` and `tally top 10` work; `tally top 0` and `tally top lots` fail with a clear message and exit 1.
- The ordering logic is not duplicated between `list` and `top`.
- The README's quick start shows it.
- Tests cover the ordering and the limit.

This issue carries the `auto-merge` label: once every reviewing role has approved the PR's current head, the implementer merges it with `weawr merge`.

issues.title: README quick start does not match the command line
issues.body:
The README's quick start says `tally count coffee`, but the command is `tally add`. A newcomer copying the first line gets `unknown command count`.

**Ask:** make the quick start true, and make it complete — every command `bin/tally.mjs` accepts appears there once, in the same style. Do not change the command line to match the README.

**Acceptance**
- Every line in the quick start runs as written and prints what the comment says.
- Nothing in `bin/` or `src/` changes.
